transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jin Park (NorthStar Head of Partnerships), Maya Singh (NorthStar Solutions Architect), Ethan Liu (NorthStar Legal Ops)

Auto-generated summary (verbatim): Intro call, partner intro, discuss integration points, security, pilot, next steps.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. With me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Jin (NorthStar): Hey Alex, doing great, thanks. Excited to chat — I'm Jin, I run partnerships at NorthStar Cloud.
00:11 Maya (NorthStar): Hi all, Maya here, solutions architect. Happy to dig into the technical bits.
00:15 Samir (SE): Hey Maya, quick heads-up i'll jump into the infra questions — we can talk latency/cost tradeoffs and network later.
00:22 Alex: Cool. High level — Redwood is a developer-first inference platform: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments (VPC/on-prem). The reason we reached out is we see an opportunity to partner — you guys have customers asking for managed LLM inference bundled with cloud services, right?
00:34 Jin: Yeah, definitely. We're seeing a lot of demand for predictable performance and cost — lots of requests from fintech and health customers for private deployments or VPC options. We want to understand how Redwood would integrate and what revenue share / reseller model might look like.
00:48 Alex: Great. We usually partner two ways: reseller/co-sell where you resell our hosted or dedicated capacity, and deeper integrations where we provide a private deployment inside your VPC with co-managed support. Both have different requirements.
01:00 Maya: On the tech side, our primary blockers are network connectivity and key management. For private deployments we need either VPC peering or PrivateLink, strict KMS integration and logs forwarded to our SIEM. We also need SOC 2/ISO artifacts. Do you guys provide per-customer KMS and audit logs?
01:20 Samir: Yes — for Redwood Private we can integrate with customer KMS and forward audit logs; there are config bits for log retention. Our product supports SAML SSO and RBAC. We have SOC 2 Type II and can share the security pack. (brief pause) Sorry, packet — pack, not packet.
01:32 Ethan (NorthStar): Great — on the legal side we'll want to see your SOC 2 report and a sample DPA. Also curious about data residency options — some clients need EU-only hosting.
01:44 Alex: We support region pinning for hosted, and Private deployments can be deployed in customer-chosen regions. We'll send SOC 2 and standard DPA.
01:51 Jin: Perfect. On the business model — how do you typically price Dedicated vs Hosted for partner-resold deals? We need ballpark numbers to propose in initial conversations.
02:05 Alex: Hosted is usage-based (per-token / per-embedding), Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. For resellers we can do a channel discount plus co-sell incentives — I'll send a sample pricing sheet.
02:16 Maya: From a technical trial perspective, we'd like to run a small benchmark: run a 7B/13B model set with 512 token sequences, target p50 latency under 200ms for gen use-case, and measure cost/TU. Is Redwood able to support benchmarking on a partner sandbox?
02:31 Samir: Definitely. We can spin up a short pilot on dedicated nodes or hosted endpoints. We'll need to agree on model family (Llama-like, MPT, etc.), input distributions, concurrency targets. Also we usually recommend quantization profiles to reduce cost — 8-bit or 4-bit depending on accuracy requirements.
02:49 Jin: Good. A couple customers care about deterministic inference for compliance — do you support model pinning and deterministic seeds?
02:57 Samir: We support model pinning and versioning; for determinism it's model dependent but we can provide reproducibility guidance. There's some noise in sampling but you can lock to specific generation settings.
03:09 Maya: Networking detail — PrivateLink vs VPC peering: PrivateLink is easier for multi-tenant hosted endpoints, peering works for private deployments. We'd prefer PrivateLink for hosted-resold. Any known limitations?
03:22 Samir: PrivateLink works fine for us; throughput limits are a thing but we can provision more endpoints or use dedicated capacity. We'll document recommended throughput per endpoint.
03:31 Jin: Competitors — a few customers asked about SageMaker and Vertex — they like integrated infra but complain about latency unpredictability and cost. How does Redwood position versus those?
03:44 Alex: We emphasize production-first SLAs and tooling: token-level cost breakdowns, traceability, and rollout controls. We also do intelligent batching & KV caching to drive down token unit economics while keeping latency SLOs.
03:58 Ethan: On contracts, we have a standard reseller MSA — we'll need to align on indemnities and security warranties. Can you share a standard reseller agreement?
04:08 Alex: Yes, we'll share a template. Small note — pricing for enterprise is often negotiated with committed throughput.
04:16 Maya: For the pilot, what telemetry will you need from us? We'll want to see traces and per-route latency dashboards.
04:25 Samir: We'll request sample prompts and traffic shape. We can instrument per-route dashboards and share Grafana / console access. We'll keep PII out of shared traces; if necessary we can mask tokens.
04:37 Jin: That sounds good. Timeline-wise, if we can get security docs and a partner deck this week, we can loop in our sales engineering to scope the pilot next week.
04:47 Alex: Sounds good. Quick clarifying question — do you want co-branded web assets or prefer an API-first approach?
04:54 Jin: Initially API-first. Down the line co-branded go-to-market could be interesting.
04:58 Alex: Great. Anything else?
05:00 Maya: One tiny nit — do you support model quantization on-host or only at deployment time? Some customers prefer artifacts pre-quantized.
05:08 Samir: We support both; we can apply quantization during model onboarding and expose quantized flavors as separate model variants. Sometimes we recommend shipping quantized variants for cost-sensitive clusters.
05:17 Ethan: From procurement — if there's a pilot, will we be able to get a short term invoice or platform credits? Some customers prefer PO-based pilots.
05:25 Alex: We can accommodate PO pilots for partners; we'll note that as a potential constraint.
05:30 [crosstalk — inaudible]
05:33 Alex: Ok let's recap. We'll send partner deck, security pack (SOC 2/DPA), sample pricing, and propose dates for a technical deep dive to scope benchmarks. Maya and Samir will own benchmark scope. Ethan will check legal/PO timelines.
05:47 Jin: Yep that works. Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
05:51 Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up with links and times. Bye.

Meeting end.

Post-call notes (auto): 
- Redwood to send partner materials (deck, pricing, SOC2, DPA)
- Technical deep-dive to be scheduled (networking + benchmark plan)
- Pilot scope: 7B/13B models, 512 tokens, target p50 <200ms, quantized variants to be evaluated
